utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is the case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I note that the parties are as before. We were supposed to continue our proceedings in this case as of today as the programme which was issued, but unfortunately, our colleague Judge Singh is still indisposed and we are unable to continue the proceedings. We have looked at the record and we find that the matters that are supposed to be continued with today are such that it wouldn't be in the interests of justice for us to continue. So we shall adjourn the proceedings until further notice. But before we rise, I wanted to find out whether there are any matters the parties would like to raise. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must address the Chamber with a piece of information about the health condition of my client, which is alarming, I must say, and it is my duty to inform the Trial Chamber thereof. He advised me that he literally collapsed in the Detention Unit last week. He had high fever, nausea, and dizziness. Medical help was asked for, but to date he has not been seen by a doctor. A nurse did come and noted that his pressure is extremely high, but the doctor still hasn't seen him. He received information last Friday by certain people in the Detention Unit. I still don't know who exactly. They told him that they tried to find a doctor but couldn't. In view of my client's age, I would really urge this Trial Chamber to use their good offices to have medical help urgently extended to my client. If you -- with your leave, Mr. Tadic himself could address the Trial Chamber himself. He came to the courtroom today primarily for this reason, to inform the Chamber of his health condition because he has not met with understanding at the appropriate instances in the Detention Unit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber can hear Mr. Tadic if he so wishes to explain. THE ACCUSED TADIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, what my counsel has said describes the situation well. On Friday, I was visited by representatives of the Detention Unit and a nurse, and they firmly promised that they would organise a doctor for Monday, which is today. However, until my departure for the courtroom, the doctor has not appeared. I spent the entire day lying down, and sometime around 1.00, the nurse came and measured my pressure again and simply told me that there is no doctor. This is a bit of a problem because I am located on a floor where Dr. Kovacevic died, and the people who were present then are still there, and they are more upset perhaps than I am. This was another reason for tempers to rise. I think that it would be reasonable to expect a doctor to be able to visit me in seven days. I am really feeling bad, and I have no reason to simulate anything. That's all I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Very well, Mr. Tadic. The Trial Chamber will take the matter up with the Registrar immediately, and the Trial Chamber will be expecting a report from the Detention Unit on the matter. At the same time, the Registrar will be requested to arrange for a medical examination and treatment, if possible, so that the Trial Chamber can be able to decide how to go about with the proceedings in your state of health. Thank you, Mr. Lukic, for raising the matter. It is indeed important that while the proceedings are pending, the health aspect of the persons in detention is looked after to the best of the resources available, and it has always been the case that doctors are requested from wherever to look after the detainees if anything comes up requiring medical attention. So the Trial Chamber will take up the matter, and the parties will be informed accordingly as to what the report will say and also whether or not any further treatment, after the initial interview with the doctor, will be required. If in the event of the condition of the accused deteriorating, the Trial Chamber will be -- will appreciate communication from the Defence counsel so that a decision can be made on what sort of examination -- medical examination to order through the Registrar's Office. The proceedings will adjourn until further notice. The parties will be notified as soon as possible once a decision has been made as to when the proceedings will resume. The Court will rise.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.27 p.m.
